title: Lipschitz-Constrained EEGNet for Safe Cross-Subject BCI Transfer
summary: This work introduces Parseval-tight frame constraints to EEGNet's convolutional layers to bound Lipschitz constants, ensuring stable predictions during cross-subject adaptation. The method modifies EEGNet's training to enforce spectral normalization while preserving its compact architecture. Evaluation measures classification accuracy and robustness on cross-subject datasets, comparing against unconstrained EEGNet and adversarially trained models.
gap: While EEGNet generalizes across subjects, its susceptibility to input variations during transfer learning remains unquantified. Existing robustness methods (e.g., Parseval networks) are untested in EEG's low-data, high-noise regime.
approach: Integrate Parseval-tight frame constraints into EEGNet's depthwise separable convolutions. Train with spectral normalization layers to limit Lipschitz constants. Retain EEG-specific feature extraction blocks.
evaluation: Baselines: vanilla EEGNet, adversarially trained EEGNet. Measures: cross-subject accuracy, Lipschitz bounds, CLEVER score. Test on BCI Competition IV datasets with leave-one-subject-out validation.
